title: Knowledge Check 2 - Lessons 6-10
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 6-10 - Solution Positioning | Data 360 Setup and Administration. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A consultant must recommend the best first use case. Which combination indicates the most sensible starting point?
options: A use case with high value but no data connected yet
A use case with clear business value, data already connected, and a measurable KPI
The most technically complex use case, to prove capability
A use case that requires every source to be unified first
questions.explanation: A good first use case balances value, data readiness, and a measurable KPI so it can succeed quickly. The high-value but no-data option is the strongest distractor, but it cannot ship, which delays proof of value.

questions.question: An analyst needs to explore unified profiles and build dashboards. Which Data 360 capability supports this analytics use case?
options: Connecting Data 360 data to a business intelligence tool such as Tableau
Triggering a real-time action
Publishing an activation to an ad platform
Building a match rule
questions.explanation: Analytics use cases are served by exposing Data 360 data to BI tools such as Tableau for reporting. Real-time actions and activations are action use cases, not analysis.

questions.question: Why is it usually a mistake to try to unify every enterprise source before delivering the first use case?
options: Unification is not supported at enterprise scale
It delays time to value and consumes credits without a proven outcome
Sources from different brands cannot be unified
It forces the use of Data Cloud One
questions.explanation: Boiling the ocean delays value and burns credits before any outcome is proven. Unification does scale and multi-brand unification is possible through data spaces, so that objection is the wrong reason.

questions.question: An admin assigns a data space to a user's permission set, but the user still cannot see the records inside it. What is the most likely cause?
options: The data space was not published
Assigning a data space grants scope but not data access; an access policy must also grant it
Data spaces cannot be assigned to users
The user needs Modify All
questions.explanation: A permission set data space assignment defines scope but does not by itself grant access to data; you create an access policy, often tag-based, to grant it. Modify All is unrelated to data space access.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes RBAC from ABAC in Data 360?
options: ABAC applies only to unstructured data
RBAC enforces row-level access, while ABAC manages feature access
RBAC governs access to features and platform capabilities, while ABAC enforces data access through policies
They are the same mechanism with different names
questions.explanation: RBAC controls who can use features and admin capabilities, while ABAC enforces object, field, and row-level data access plus masking through policies. Reversing them is the classic distractor.

questions.question: A policy must hide PII fields from all users except a compliance group. Which approach best fits?
options: Delete the fields in the source system
Rely on page layouts to hide the fields
Remove the fields from the data model
Tag the fields, classify them as PII, and bind a masking or access policy to the tag
questions.explanation: Data 360 attaches policies to tags, so tagging and classifying the fields and binding a policy grants context-aware access or masking. Removing fields from the model would break downstream use cases and is far too blunt.

questions.question: A marketer activates a segment that must exclude customers who opted out of marketing. How does Data 360 enforce this?
options: Consent is enforced only in the destination channel
Consent-aware activation evaluates flags such as Do Not Sell or Email Opt-Out and excludes non-consented records before sharing
Consent cannot be enforced at activation
Consent is enforced by deleting the segment
questions.explanation: At activation, Data 360 evaluates consent flags and automatically excludes records that violate them, so enforcement happens before sharing. The strongest distractor places enforcement only in the channel and misses platform-level enforcement.

questions.question: A customer exercises a GDPR right to erasure. What is the recommended way to submit the request in Data 360?
options: Exclude the customer from all segments
Delete the record manually in CRM only
Submit the data subject rights request through the Salesforce Consent API
Set the record's consent flag to opt-out
questions.explanation: Data subject rights requests, including the right to be forgotten, are submitted through the Salesforce Consent API and cover Data 360 as well as CRM. Manual CRM deletion misses the Data 360 data.

questions.question: Which list best reflects Salesforce's Trusted AI principles?
options: Unification, Activation, Segmentation, Insights
Zero Copy, Data Cloud One, Data Spaces, Credits
Speed, Scale, Cost, Coverage
Accuracy, Safety, Transparency, Empowerment, Sustainability
questions.explanation: Salesforce's Trusted AI principles are Accuracy, Safety, Transparency, Empowerment, and Sustainability. The product-feature option confuses Data 360 capabilities with ethics principles.

questions.question: An admin assigns the Data Cloud User permission set to a business analyst, but the analyst reports they cannot open Data Cloud Setup. What is the reason?
options: The analyst also needs the System Administrator profile
Data Cloud User grants view-only access and no Data Cloud Setup access
The analyst's permission set license expired overnight
Data Cloud User requires the Modify All Data permission
questions.explanation: Data Cloud User is a view-only set with no Data Cloud Setup access, so it cannot open the admin console. The strongest distractor, requiring the System Administrator profile, is wrong because the analyst was never meant to administrate; the correct set for build work is Data Cloud Architect.

questions.question: An architect must give a developer every Data 360 capability but keep them out of broad Salesforce Setup changes. What is the best approach?
options: Assign Data Cloud User
Assign Data Cloud Architect exactly as shipped
Clone Data Cloud Architect and remove the Customize Application permission before assigning
Create a brand new permission set from scratch
questions.explanation: Data Cloud Architect grants full Data 360 access but also bundles Customize Application, so cloning it and stripping that one permission preserves the capability while limiting Setup reach. Assigning it as shipped is the strongest distractor and is wrong because it hands over broad Setup customization.

questions.question: An org moved from a Customer Data Platform license to a Data Cloud license and users lost Data 360 access. What must the admin do?
options: Nothing, access carries over with the license
Assign the permission sets associated with the new Data Cloud license
Recreate every affected user record
Grant the System Administrator profile to everyone
questions.explanation: The old Customer Data Platform permission sets stop granting Data 360 access after the license change, so the new Data Cloud permission sets must be assigned, ideally in bulk with User Access Policies. Granting System Administrator to everyone is the strongest distractor and is wrong because it over-grants and bypasses the intended permission model.

questions.question: A business wants to segregate two brands' data inside one Data 360 instance but holds only the standard Data Cloud license. What is true?
options: The standard license includes unlimited data spaces
The standard license includes only the default data space, and more require the Data Spaces add-on
Data spaces are unnecessary because each brand is a separate org
The data space prefix can be changed at any time
questions.explanation: Standard Data Cloud and Customer Data Platform licenses include only the default data space, so additional spaces need the Data Spaces add-on license. The distractor about separate orgs is wrong because a data space is a partition inside one Data 360 instance, not a distinct tenant.

questions.question: An admin created a data space with prefix BR1 and now wants to rename it to BR2. What is the correct statement?
options: Change the prefix in the Feature Manager
Rename it in Data Spaces and the change propagates automatically
The prefix cannot be changed after save because it is part of object API names
Delete and recreate the space with no impact on dependent objects
questions.explanation: The prefix is fixed at save because it is embedded in API names of objects that live in multiple data spaces. Deleting and recreating is the strongest distractor and is wrong because objects already depend on the space, which blocks deletion.

questions.question: A team cannot see a specific connector as a source option in the connection wizard, though other connectors work. What should the admin check first?
options: The data space prefix
The user's locale setting
The user's profile
Whether the connector feature is enabled in the Feature Manager
questions.explanation: Beta and AI connectors must be enabled in the Feature Manager before their type appears in the connection wizard. Changing the profile is the strongest distractor and is wrong because the wizard content is governed by org feature enablement, not by the user's profile.
